lesson.summary: Derive classes from a base class and reuse what it already does.

payload.markdown: Inheritance is the means by which one or more classes can be derived from a base class.

blocks.text: Inheritance is the means by which one or more classes can be derived from a base class.

payload.markdown: A class that inherits from another is said to be a subclass of it. This relationship is often described in terms of parents and children. A child class is derived from and inherits characteristics from the parent. These characteristics consist of both properties and methods. The child class will typically add new functionality to that provided by its parent (also known as a superclass); for this reason, a child class is said to extend its parent.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Inheritance: Deriving a class from a base class to reuse and specialise its behaviour.
Properties & Methods: Class state held in properties, and behaviour implemented as methods.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Dynamic Properties: Creating properties by assignment instead of declaration; deprecated since PHP 8.
Magic Methods: __construct, __get, __toString and friends that the engine invokes for you.
Typed Properties: Declaring property types so invalid object state is rejected early.
